area: Impact feel: hitstop, screen shake, vibration

items.title: Victim-hit hitstop: whole-world 3-tick (~200ms) freeze + red edge vignette
items.claim: Canon hitstop (Sakurai/Smash) freezes ONLY the attacker+victim pair, scales duration with damage (Ultimate: d*0.65+6 frames, capped 30), and lets the rest of the world keep running. The OG measurably does something DIFFERENT: when the player takes a hit, the ENTIRE world (strokes, background, HUD bars) freezes pixel-identical for 3 content ticks (~200ms) under a red edge vignette — fixed length, not damage-scaled, global scope. Coincidentally this equals Vlambeer's recommended 0.2s 'sleep', but the OG's global scope is the spec, not the canon's pair-only scope.

sources.title: "Thinking About Hitstop" — Sakurai's Famitsu Column Vol. 490-1 (Source Gaming translation)
Jan Willem Nijman (Vlambeer) — The Art of Screenshake (INDIGO 2013)

items.adjudication_reason: Ledger §S24-F 'Global hit-stop' row: 'the ENTIRE world froze 3 content ticks (~200 ms) under a red edge vignette ... a real engine beat, chaos-testable.' Repo has NO hitstop today — DuelScene's damage-to-player branch only calls spawnBlood + startOgSlash('enemy'). Use the measured params (global, fixed 3 ticks = 12 sim steps at 60Hz), never Sakurai's damage-scaled pair-only model.
items.implementation_note: Freeze is gameplay-visible, so it belongs in Sim (src/core) as a hold counter armed by the damage-to-player event, with the tick count in src/config tagged MEASURED (§S24-F); DuelScene renders the red edge vignette during the hold. Chaos-test per the ledger's own note: plant a moving stroke, assert pixel-static world during the 12 steps.

items.title: Attacker-hit hitstop (player LANDS a hit): unobserved — measure before adding
items.claim: Sakurai's rule is that hitstop fires on EVERY connect, freezing both parties equally — canon says player-dealt hits should also stop time. But the ledger only ever measured the freeze when the PLAYER TOOK a hit; whether the world freezes when the player's slash lands on an enemy was never checked. §S24-E's landing holds (mid-combo hit = 4–5 ticks attacker recovery, E1/E11) are pose holds on the attacker animation, NOT a verified world freeze — background/bars were not asserted pixel-static in those windows.

sources.title: "Thinking About Hitstop" — Sakurai's Famitsu Column Vol. 490-1 (Source Gaming translation)

items.adjudication_reason: Ledger §S24-F records the freeze ONLY for 'when the A28 player took a hit'; §S24-E partb 'Landing holds' rows (E1: 4 ticks; E11: 4–5 with +47 px recoil drift) describe attacker pose recovery, not a background-verified world freeze. Adopting Sakurai's every-connect rule unmeasured would be fidelity divergence.
items.implementation_note: Cheap measurement: take an existing player-dealt hit tick (e.g. §S24-E E1 flash window), diff background/HUD pixels across the 4–5 hold ticks exactly as §S24-F did for the victim case. If frozen → extend item 1's hold to both directions; if moving → attacker 'hitstop' is animation-hold only, already covered by §S24-E landing holds.

items.title: Screen shake and controller vibration: canon staples the OG does not have
items.claim: Vlambeer's talk makes screenshake the signature juice trick, and Jiesang Song recommends camera shake plus controller rumble as first-line impact fixes. The OG shows NEITHER: zero shake observations across the entire measurement corpus despite §S24-G's traps documenting exact camera/parallax anchoring analysis (fixed screen overlays at dx=0, 0.73× parallax layers) that would have caught any camera displacement; and it is a mouse-driven Flash browser game with no haptics channel at all. Adding either is a fidelity DEFECT under the prime directive.

sources.title: Jan Willem Nijman (Vlambeer) — The Art of Screenshake (INDIGO 2013)
The Art of Screenshake — talk summary with the 0.2s sleep + shake tricks
Jiesang Song — Improving the Combat 'Impact' of Action Games (Game Developer/Gamasutra)

items.adjudication_reason: grep of COMBAT_MEASUREMENTS.md returns zero 'shake' rows while §S24-G traps #9 prove the corpus tracked camera anchoring precisely (the mushroom-cluster dx=0 fixed overlay, 0.73× boulder parallax) — shake would have registered; src/ also has no shake code to remove (grep clean). No vibration row exists; input model is mouse strokes per §S24-C ('any drawn stroke = slash').
items.implementation_note: Nothing to build — this item exists to block future 'juice it up' churn. If a later video pass ever finds a shake instance, reopen as MEASURE_FIRST.

items.title: Per-hit full-screen red wash / hurt vignette on damage taken (3–5 ticks)
items.claim: Song's canon endorses screen flash and hit lighting as impact feedback; the OG has its own measured version: a full-screen red WASH (scene visible through it) fires per player-HP drop for 3–5 content ticks per burst — 7 bursts tracked against HP drops, and 2 kills produced NO wash (kills get blood/hat/jug VFX instead). e-5.2 pins the same phenomenon as the ~0.20s player-hurt vignette (red tint, scene still in colour), distinct from the kill-cam's red+black-silhouette screen. It co-occurs with the 3-tick freeze of item 1.

sources.title: Jiesang Song — Improving the Combat 'Impact' of Action Games (screen flash, hit lighting)
The Art of Screenshake — talk summary (impact feedback layering)

items.adjudication_reason: Ledger §S24-F 'Full-screen red WASH = player-took-damage feedback (3–5 ticks/burst ... 2 kills with NO wash) — reconfirms e-5.2'. Repo has NO per-hit wash: DuelScene's damage-to-player branch spawns blood only. Wire it to the existing `ev.type === 'damage' && ev.target === 'player'` drain branch; render like the killBeat fillRect overlay; constants MEASURED-tagged in src/config/fx.ts (per src/config/CLAUDE.md labeling rule).
items.implementation_note: One overlay, two zones per the ledger: full-screen tint at wash alpha + stronger edges (the 'red edge vignette' under the freeze). Duration 3–5 content ticks (~200–333ms) on the fx clock. Explicitly suppress it on the kill event — 2 measured kills had no wash; the kill-cam owns that beat.

items.title: Existing persistent low-HP vignette is INFERRED and possibly a divergence
items.claim: DuelScene currently draws a permanent red edge vignette that ramps in below 50% HP (SYNTHESIS §4 seed). The measurement corpus never records a persistent low-HP tint — every measured red overlay is EVENT-driven (per-hit vignette/wash ~0.20s, kill-cam). If the OG has no standing low-HP vignette, the current one is generic-canon juice masquerading as fidelity; if it does, its threshold and alpha need measuring. Cannot adjudicate the render without a frame check at low player HP with no recent hit.

sources.title: Jiesang Song — Improving the Combat 'Impact' of Action Games (hit lighting is momentary, not persistent)

items.adjudication_reason: DuelScene.drawHud comment 'Low-HP red vignette: ramps from 50% HP (SYNTHESIS §4)' has no MEASURED backing; ledger e-5.2 and §S24-F describe only transient per-hit vignettes/washes. The e-4/e-5.1 beach-duel window (player at 4/20 HP, t≈1963) is an already-catalogued frame range to check for a standing tint between hits.
items.implementation_note: Pull 2–3 stills from the beach duel at 4/20 HP several ticks after the last wash burst; diff screen edges against a full-HP frame. Absent → delete the drawHud vignette block (simplest change wins); present → replace the INFERRED 50%/0.4-alpha ramp with measured values.

items.title: Kill beat: replace INFERRED slow-mo FINISHER_FLASH with the measured hard-cut kill-cam timeline
items.claim: Song's canon recommends slow motion before climactic attacks — and the OG demonstrably does NOT use it. The measured kill-cam (B05 archer kill) is all hard cuts: fatal contact (cyan Chi burst at contact point) → +2 ticks HARD CUT (no fade) to a red screen with BLACK SILHOUETTES → loser's death replayed in silhouette settling in 16 ticks → YOU WIN text +17 ticks after onset → ~74 ticks (~4.9s) total → hard cut to loot. The repo's current kill beat (420ms red flash + 0.35× slow-mo ramp + 900ms hold, then result scene) is an invented canon-flavored beat that contradicts every measured element.

sources.title: Jiesang Song — Improving the Combat 'Impact' of Action Games (slow-motion as canon; OG diverges)
"Thinking About Hitstop" — Sakurai's Famitsu Column (impact emphasis via freeze, not slow-mo)

items.adjudication_reason: src/config/fx.ts FINISHER_FLASH is explicitly INFERRED (slowMoScale 0.35, slowMoRampMs 90) and DuelScene's killBeat path applies it plus a 900ms hold — all contradicted by ledger §S24-F 'Kill-cam timeline (B05)': hard cut at +2 ticks, red+black silhouettes, YOU WIN +17 ticks, ~74 ticks total, no slow-mo, no fade. e-5.2 already corrected the related kill-flash/hurt-vignette conflation.
items.implementation_note: Re-parameterize FINISHER_FLASH to the measured tick timeline (MEASURED tags, dual-entry in tests/config-values.test.ts per the ratchet); drop the slow-mo scale entirely — remember src/game/CLAUDE.md's stuck-timescale landmine when removing it. Silhouette render = existing fighter pose drawn in solid black over the red field; loser collapse replay is P5-adjacent (death anim is 38 recorded frames per DuelScene comment) so the timeline skeleton can ship first with the held final pose.

items.title: Measured hit-reaction displacements: launcher, knockdown, knockback (Sim-owned, not render juice)
items.claim: Song's first principle — every attack must produce a visible damage reaction — is the one canon item the OG fully embodies, with exact numbers: small hits (−7/−12 HP) displace ~0; big hits (−17..−19) displace 40–270px; knock-up LAUNCHER ~270px vertical (x static, lands in 7 ticks); KNOCKDOWN prone tumble +136–186px (stands by ~6 ticks); knockback slide −188px + skid settle; victims displace toward the attacker's ORIGIN side as the attacker passes through (KB-RULE). These are gameplay-state displacements, not camera tricks — they belong in the Sim.

sources.title: Jiesang Song — Improving the Combat 'Impact' of Action Games (damage-motion principle)
Hitlag — SmashWiki (knockback as sim-state, distinct from hitlag)

items.adjudication_reason: Ledger §S24-F 'Hit reactions on the player (Honda window)' + §S24-C P-LEGS catalogue (knock-up ~270px vertical; knockdown +136–186px; knockbacks −188/+40px; ≤42px settles) — while DuelScene's both damage branches read 'No transcribed hit-stagger yet (P5)' and the Sim applies no hit displacement. Positions are sim state, so per src/game/CLAUDE.md this cannot live in the scene.
items.implementation_note: Constants in src/config tagged MEASURED (per-reaction displacement, tick counts, KB-RULE direction = toward attacker origin side); selection rule (small hit → 0, big hit → reaction class) is only medium-confidence, so tag the threshold INFERRED. Core logic in Sim with injected RNG only; DuelScene just renders the resulting positions plus the P5 poses later.

dead_ends: No developer postmortem, GDC talk, or technical writeup specific to Straw Hat Samurai: Duels' impact effects exists anywhere findable — all OG juice parameters come exclusively from the project's own frame measurements (§S24-F), which is why every ADAPT re-parameterizes canon to ledger values. Sakurai's translated column itself contains no concrete frame numbers (only the pair-freeze/damage-scaling/cap principles); the numeric formulas had to come from SmashWiki, which documents Smash, not SHSD — cited only to show how far the OG's global fixed-length freeze diverges from genre canon. 'Screen shake' produced zero hits in the measurement ledger, MASTER_SPEC grep, and src/ grep — its absence is an inference from a corpus that demonstrably tracked camera anchoring (§S24-G trap #9), not a positive measurement; flagged as such in item 3. The Gamasutra original URL (gamasutra.com/view/feature/130703) redirects; the Game Developer mirror was fetched instead.
